entry.title: CANTraj: Recovering Vehicle Trajectories from CAN Signals in Naturalistic Driving
entry.summary:
Open driving releases and usage-based insurance programs often claim to prevent privacy breaches by omitting GPS records when sharing or collecting vehicle data. However, removing GPS coordinates from driving logs does not erase the location information carried by vehicle signals. While prior route-inference attacks have demonstrated that speed, steering, and driving events can be matched to road networks to reconstruct trajectories, existing studies rely on inconsistent prior assumptions and evaluation metrics and are tested only on small, restricted datasets, making their results difficult to compare and their real-world effectiveness uncertain.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #cryptography #databases

entry.title: How rigid is maximum cardinality search? Stability and locality of MCS orderings under edge updates, verified in Lean
entry.summary:
For which sets F of edge modifications do a graph G and the modified graph share a maximum cardinality search (MCS) ordering? We prove that they do whenever, along every proper common MCS prefix, each unchosen vertex's neighbour count in the second graph exceeds its count in the first by zero or one. In particular, inserting or deleting any matching, or flipping a single edge, preserves a common ordering, and under the same hypothesis every common MCS prefix extends to a full common ordering without backtracking.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #algorithms #logic

entry.title: DeCompCert: A Verified Decompiler for CompCert-Generated AArch64. DeCompCert is a Rocq-verified decompiler for AArch64 assembly generated by CompCert.
entry.summary:
DeCompCert is a Rocq-verified decompiler for AArch64 assembly generated by CompCert. It reconstructs CompCert C through nine reverse passes, combining deductively verified transformations with translation validation. Untrusted OCaml and Datalog analyses propose candidate reconstructions, while verified validators accept only candidates that satisfy the required semantic correspondence.

Source: arXiv CS (PL, SE, DB, DC, DS) · Tags: #compilers #distributed-systems #cryptography #rust

entry.title: The Pipes Model for Latency and Throughput Analysis
entry.summary:
In much of the distributed computing literature, latency is expressed as the number of communication rounds or network delays; such metrics do not directly account for the amount of data sent or the dependencies among parties sending the data. Throughput is also normally evaluated empirically. As a consequence, the standard models used for analysing state machine replication (SMR) protocols do not by themselves provide an end-to-end analytical comparison of practical latency and throughput as functions of per-processor bandwidth and transaction arrival rate.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #distributed-systems
